back: A huge body of air with roughly uniform temperature and humidity, gained over its source region.
Tropical (T, warm) or polar (P, cold); maritime (m, moist) or continental (c, dry): mT, cT, mP, cP.
A large uniform land or sea area, usually under calm high pressure, where an air mass forms.
Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone: low-pressure belt where trade winds converge and rise, giving heavy rain.
January: south of the equator over southern Africa. July: north, over West Africa and the Sahel (about 15-20° N).
Moist air from the Indian Ocean; summer moisture, and guti on the Eastern Highlands in the cool season.
Moist air from the northern Indian Ocean, reaching northern Zimbabwe in the southern summer.
Warm, very moist, unstable air from the Congo basin; heavy, widespread mid-summer rain.
High pressure over southern Africa: sinking dry air, clear skies, cold nights.
